story_type: heavy icebreaker smashes a channel through Antarctic fast ice
hook: A 48-year-old ship smashing a road through Antarctic ice.
narration: This forty eight year old ship was smashing a road through Antarctic ice.
The Coast Guard cutter Polar Star is three hundred ninety nine feet long and weighs thirteen thousand tons.
It had sailed from Seattle to McMurdo Station, the largest station on the continent.
Its job is to break a channel through miles of ice, some of it twenty one feet thick.
An icebreaker rarely slices through. Its rounded bow rides up onto the ice, and the ship's weight crushes it from above.
When the ice will not give, the crew backs up and rams it again.
[short pause] That season, Polar Star broke thirty five nautical miles of fast ice, from the ice pier out to the Ross Sea.
The channel would let two supply ships bring in more than a thousand cargo containers and eight million gallons of fuel.
outcome: After three weeks of breaking ice, Polar Star and its crew arrived at McMurdo Station.
title: Icebreaker smashes a road to Antarctica
description:
In January 2024 the Coast Guard cutter Polar Star broke a channel through 35 nautical miles of fast ice in McMurdo Sound for Operation Deep Freeze, so supply ships could reach McMurdo Station, Antarctica.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Jeremy Burgess and Petty Officer 2nd Class Ryan Graves, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/913139/coast-guard-cutter-polar-star-wagb-10-break-ice-during-operation-deep-freeze-24

extra_sources.excerpt: The U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Polar Star (WAGB 10) and crew arrived at McMurdo Station in Antarctica, Jan. 16, following the cutter’s departure from its Seattle homeport Nov. 15.

Each year, the crew takes the 399-foot, 13,000-ton cutter south to break a navigable channel through miles of ice, sometimes as much as 21-feet thick, to allow fuel and supply ships to reach McMurdo Station, the U.S. Antarctic Program’s logistics hub and the largest station on the continent.

had commenced breaking 35 nautical miles of fast ice that extended from the ice pier in Winter Quarters Bay at McMurdo Station out to the Ross Sea. Polar Star spent three weeks breaking ice to make the initial cut for the shipping channel.
The cleared channel to McMurdo Station will enable two supply vessels, Ocean Gladiator and Arcadia Trade, to offload more than 1,000 cargo containers and 8 million gallons of fuel.
The crew dedicates countless hours year-round preparing the 48-year-old ship for this critical mission and I could not ask for a more capable, dedicated team.
U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Polar Star (WAGB 10) breaks through the fast ice by backing and ramming in the McMurdo Sound, Antarctica, Jan 5, 2024.
